title: people-ops-q1-q2-2026-self-notes-and-manager-prep
body:
Purpose: quick, messy scratchpad for my upcoming 1:1 and mid-cycle check. Not polished — notes to self, wins, weak spots, and concrete asks for manager.

High-level summary (30s):
- Focus: reduce time-to-hire for IC engineering roles and stabilize onboarding funnel metrics.
- Progress: piloted interview panel rubric (eng-sre + eng-serving-runtime) — panel score variance down ~18% in pilot group.
- Risk: Hiring demand continues to outpace pipeline; need capacity and better sourcing strategy for backend/infra.

Quarterly goals (Q1–Q2 2026) — working draft:
1) Time-to-hire (offer accepted): reduce from 64 days -> 45 days for SWE-IC roles.
   - Tactics: tighten ATS stages, create 2-week recruiter + hiring manager SLAs, weekly sourcing blitz for priority roles.
   - Measurement: ATS report (pipeline_start -> offer_accepted) each Monday.
2) Improve onboarding activation: increase new-hire 30-day activation (first PR + passed checklist) from 72% -> 90%.
   - Tactics: onboarding concierge pilot (buddy + infra checklist + preprovisioning).
3) Diversity: increase underrepresented grp candidates in pipeline to 35% for RN rounds for infra/serving-runtime roles.
   - Tactics: targeted sourcing, partnerships, referral incentives.
4) Ops stability: reduce recruiter handoff errors (lost docs/missed interview prep) to <=2/month.

Recent wins / evidence:
- Interview rubric pilot (Dec–Jan): created rubric + training slides, ran 6 panels, post-pilot survey says 78% of interviewers found rubric easier. Panel score variance decreased ~18% (pilot sample).
- Onboarding checklist consolidated into single doc and automated reminder (Slack) — early metrics show first PR increased for pilot cohort (n=12) from 58% -> 83% in 30 days.
- Negotiation toolkit updated: fewer counteroffers escalations last month (n small, but promising).

Open risks / blockers:
- Sourcing shortage for infra SWE (high bar + market). Need temporary vendor / agency support or hiring event budget.
- Engineering hiring managers still inconsistent on calendar hygiene — interviews canceled late, causing delays.
- Headcount forecast for H2 uncertain; if hiring pace stops, some projects (onboarding concierge) may not get enough runway.

Concrete asks for manager (1:1):
- Approval to run a 2-week hiring event budget (~$6k) to bring in 8 screened candidates for infra/serving-runtime roles. Rationale: expensive but concentrated and proven in past cycles.
- Help nudge ENG leadership to enforce interview scheduling windows + cancellation policy. Suggest exec email and a short guide posted to Confluence.
- Support to pilot temporary contract sourcer (1 FTE equivalent) for 8 weeks.
- Feedback on rubric — want permission to roll out company-wide in March if you OK.

Notes for calibration / self-eval (mid-cycle):
- Strengths: cross-team facilitation, pragmatic ops focus, data-driven iteration (small pilots first).
- Areas to improve: stakeholder comms — sometimes I assume too much context and skip explicit updates; need to send weekly 1-page status to ENG leads.
- Stretch goal: design and own the first 90-day new hire activation dashboard in the Console (coordinate with observability/product).

Specific manager discussion points (order):
1) Budget approvals (hiring event + sourcer) — automated follow-up doc prepared (link in linked_artifacts).
2) Rubric rollout timeline and expectation setting for hiring managers.
3) H2 headcount signal: ask for earliest signal date and any draft org priorities from ENG leadership.
4) Career path ask: request guidance on leveling to Senior People Ops (impact examples, key metrics to show).
5) Blocker: ask for support to have SRE lead join monthly hiring sync for on-call/infra candidate bar alignment.

Draft talking scripts for 1:1 (concise):
- "Quick update: rubric pilot showed lower variance and better interviewer confidence — I'd like to roll company-wide in March; I need your OK and a short communication to ENG leads."
- "Budget ask: I'm proposing $6k for a concentrated hiring event to get 6–8 vetted infra candidates — we expect at least 1 hire and 2 strong runner-ups; is that doable within our Q1 flex budget?"

Feedback snippets to remember (copied from Slack & pilot survey):
- "Rubric actually made interviews feel less scattershot" — Riley Chen
- "Onboarding reminders helped me get infra access faster" — new hire (pilot cohort)
- "Could use more interview prep time for panelists" — Marcus Diaz (panelist)

To-dos (next 2 weeks):
- Finalize hiring event brief + cost breakdown (due Friday).
- Draft exec note about interview cancellation policy (own this; send for manager signoff).
- Build week-1 dashboard mock for onboarding activation (coordinate with console-and-rollouts team).
- Share rubric and training slides with ENG leads (target Wed).

Personal development notes:
- Want to practice concise stakeholder updates (weekly 1-page). Plan: subscribe to "Exec Summary" workshop in internal L&D (register by end of Feb).
- Shadow Marcus for 1 hiring panel per month to keep bar alignment.

Misc messy notes / scratch ideas:
- Could we add a lightweight "candidate concierge" automation: re-use preprovisioning scripts so infra access ready on day 0? Reach out to infra-release-eng teams.
- Consider rotating interview panel membership to reduce interviewer fatigue.

Version history / context:
- Nov 2025: first sketch of onboarding concierge idea.
- Dec 2025–Jan 2026: rubric pilot + onboarding pilot executed.
- Feb 2026: preparing mid-cycle check-in and budget asks.

If manager agrees: next steps timeline (tentative)
- Mar 1: company-wide rollout of rubric training (if ok).
- Mar 8–22: hiring event (if budget approved).
- Apr: onboarding concierge full pilot (scale to 30 hires)

Notes-to-self: keep this doc private (personal scratchpad). Move to shared/people-ops only if manager asks for artifacts for review.

End of notes.
